body: Root cause was NOT the S170-05 nav-chrome bug -- a distinct dead-code bug: reComplete (a properly proximity-scoped regex) was defined but never referenced; the switch statement checked completion-verb presence and buyback-word presence independently with no proximity requirement, so any completion word anywhere in a 20KB press release was enough. Confirmed live: a customer-retention marketing release and a proxy-vote release's boilerplate both misclassified as real buyback completions. Also fixed: reBuybackCore too loose (bare 'repurchase' matched irrelevant/repo-financing uses), reAuthorize/reComplete proximity windows too tight for real prose (missed a genuine CAE NCIB renewal entirely), extractUSD/extractShares picked the first dollar figure anywhere in the document with no proximity to the buyback mention (Docusign's real figure 17.5M vs first-in-doc unrelated revenue 30.2M), and comparison-year figures (' compared to  last year') could win over the real current-period figure. 6 new regression tests using real captured press-release text. Corrected the live entity-graph: removed 8 fabricated/no-longer-qualifying signals, corrected 2 real signals' amounts (TOUR, CAE). Regenerated var/buybacks/buybacks.ndjson (14->4 records) by reclassifying the original 14 records' real bodies through the fixed classifier. Rebuilt + restarted the live fatbaby-buyback-watcher.service. Commit 9554f4c.
title: buyback-watcher: dead-code proximity bug + 3 related classification/extraction bugs (S170-06)
